info.title: Attome XRM API
info.description: The Attome XRM platform's HTTP API. Entity record shapes under `/api/v1/{entity}` are resolved from each deployment's runtime metadata (D-003) and therefore cannot be enumerated statically — those operations document the generic envelope only. Fetch `GET /api/v1/schema/{logicalname}` for a live entity's fields.

get.description: The portfolio's figures rolled up from its programmes and their projects, computed when read.

404.description: No such portfolio, or not visible to this caller

get.description: The programme's figures rolled up from its projects, computed when read.

404.description: No such program, or not visible to this caller

post.description:
Approves the change request through the four-eyes gate: when the approval policy requires it, this
submits an approval request a second person decides; otherwise it applies now. Audited.

404.description: No such change request, or not visible to this caller

422.description: The transition's guard refused it (the caller requested this change request)

post.description: Rejects the change request, through the same four-eyes gate as approving. Audited.

404.description: No such change request, or not visible to this caller

422.description: The transition's guard refused it (the caller requested this change request)

post.summary: Sends a change request for the customer's signature.
post.description:
The change document goes to the signer in a K4 envelope; when it is
signed the change request is approved and the project rebaselined, and a
declined envelope rejects it.

404.description: No such change request or document, or sign-off is not installed

409.description: Not pending, not customer facing, or already out for sign-off

post.description:
Approves a submitted timesheet through the four-eyes gate, so its period is locked; when the
approval policy requires it, a second person decides. Audited.

404.description: No such timesheet, or not visible to this caller

409.description: Not submitted, already decided, or changed concurrently

422.description: The transition's guard refused it (the caller owns this timesheet)

post.description: Sends a submitted timesheet back, through the same four-eyes gate as approving. Audited.

404.description: No such timesheet, or not visible to this caller

409.description: Not submitted, already decided, or changed concurrently

422.description: The transition's guard refused it (the caller owns this timesheet)

post.description:
Moves the owner's timesheet from draft to submitted for review; no approval gate applies to one's
own submission. Audited.

404.description: No such timesheet, or not visible to this caller

post.description:
Saves a snapshot of the project's work-item schedule that later progress is compared with;
baselines are never changed. Audited.

200.description: A baseline with this label already existed for this project; returned as-is

404.description: No such project, or not visible to this caller

409.description: Another capture for this project is already in progress

422.description: label is empty, or trigger is not one of initial/change_request/manual

get.summary: What a project's Gantt chart draws.
get.description:
The work items with dates and critical-path float, their dependencies,
and the latest baseline's planned dates for the overlay.

200.description: Work items, dependencies and the latest baseline

404.description: No such project, or not visible to this caller

get.description:
The control centre tiles, computed live: health, weighted progress, budget consumed, open risks
and pending approvals.

404.description: No such project, or not visible to this caller

get.description:
The work-item tree with each phase's progress weighted by points, computed when read; nothing is
stored on the parent.

404.description: No such project, or not visible to this caller

post.summary: Proposes an invoice for a project.
post.description:
A milestone invoices one accepted deliverable; time and materials
invoices the billable approved hours not yet proposed. Billing makes the
draft invoice; a repeat never proposes the same work twice.

404.description: No such project, or project invoicing is not installed

422.description: No account, an unaccepted deliverable or an unknown kind

post.summary: Checks a spend against the project's budget line.
post.description:
The line is the finance budget line linked to the project; the answer
says whether the spend fits, warns or is blocked by the line's setting.

200.description: Whether the spend fits the project's budget line

404.description: No such project, or budgets are not installed

422.description: No budget line, or not an amount

x-audit-exempt.note: answers whether a spend fits the budget line; writes nothing

get.description:
Per resource and period: the capacity there is, how much is allocated, how much was logged, and
whether the resource is over-committed. Computed when read.

parameters.name: team
parameters.description:
Restrict to resources on this `team.id` — also the
authorization gate for a `Team`-tier caller; see this module's doc
comment.

parameters.name: skill
parameters.description: Restrict to resources holding this `resource_skill.skill` value.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based: page 1 is the first page.

403.description: Caller lacks the required privilege, or the requested team is outside their scope

422.description: from is after to, or paging is out of range

label.description:
A human name for this snapshot (e.g. "Sprint 3 baseline"). Capturing
twice with the same label for the same project is safe — see this
module's doc comment — and returns the existing baseline rather than
creating a duplicate.

item_count.description:
Number of `project_baseline_item` rows captured under this
baseline — every active work item on the project at capture time.

approval_pending.description:
`true` when this call only submitted a pending four-eyes approval
request rather than deciding the change request immediately —
mirrors `attome-dashboard::lifecycle::PublishResponse`'s own field.

ErrorDetails.description:
`ErrorResponse.details`: its shape depends on the `error` code —
a list of [`FieldError`] on `validation_error`, [`RuleViolationDetails`] on
`rule_violation`, [`FieldLockedDetails`] on `field_locked` and
`field_locked_required` (D-789).

ErrorResponse.description: Standard error envelope. `error` is a stable machine-readable code; `message` is human-readable and never contains internal detail.

current_state.description:
Present on a version conflict: the server's current row for the
fields the caller touched, as a JSON object. The owning engine filters
sensitive columns out before building it (BTY-16c's precondition), so
this is a deliberate filtered projection — never a raw row dump.

current_version.description:
Present on a version conflict: the `row_version` the server currently
holds, so a caller can re-read and retry instead of guessing what the
winner wrote. Omitted when the conflict is not version-based.

oneOf.description:
Structured detail, shaped by `error` (see [`ErrorDetails`]): every
field-level failure on a `validation_error` response when the raiser
has a field list, so a form can render them all at once; every firing
rule on a `rule_violation` response from a business rule; every
refused field on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`. Omitted
otherwise.

error.description:
Stable machine-readable code — `not_found`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`,
`attribute_not_writable`, `limit_exceeded`,
`conflict`, `version_conflict`, `duplicate_detected`, `idempotency_conflict`,
`validation_error`, `customer_tests_failed`, `feature_unavailable`, `feature_hidden`,
`rate_limit_exceeded`, `overloaded`, `capability_unavailable`,
`metadata_authoring_locked`, `transition_not_allowed`,
`rule_violation`, `field_locked`, `field_locked_required`,
`reauth_required`, `server_timeout`, `query_timeout`, `read_only`, `payload_too_large`,
`request_rejected`, `invalid_cursor`, `resync_needed`, `cascade_restricted`,
`idempotency_outcome_unknown`, `idempotency_replay_unavailable`,
`method_not_allowed`, or
`internal_error` — one per `AppError` variant (`FieldLocked` answers
two: plain and required) (`attome-types/src/error.rs`); M01 Core C-23
found this list four codes short of the taxonomy it documents.

errors.description:
Every field-level failure on a `validation_error`, as
`{attribute, rule, message, fix}`.

field.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the first
refused field (every one is in `details.fields`); on
`attribute_not_writable` (Q15-T4): the attribute the caller may not
write.

hidden.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected`: how many more matches the caller may
not read.

instance.description: The request path the problem happened at.

matches.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected` (A15-T4): the existing records the
save matches that the caller may read (record, rule, score).

request_id.description:
Present on responses that passed through the request-id middleware
(D-043); absent on the few pre-middleware rejection paths.

retry_after_sec.description:
Present on a `rate_limit_exceeded` response when the limiter knows its
window: seconds to wait before retrying, equal by construction to the
`Retry-After` header on the same response (BTY-11a). Omitted when the
limit that was hit has no known window.

retryable.description:
Whether the same request may succeed later (the error catalogue's
verdict for `code`).

rule_id.description:
Present on a `rule_violation` response (D-472): the id of the
`xrm_core_rule` whose failing expression produced this 422, so a
client can highlight or re-check the exact rule without parsing
`message`. Omitted on every other code, and on any response that
does not name a rule.
Also present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the
business rule that locks `field`.

rule_name.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`: the display name
of the rule that locks `field`.

title.description:
A short title for `code` in the request's language (Z14-T3), e.g.
`The resource was not found.`

type.description: Z14-T1 (RFC 9457): `about:blank`; the problem is named by `code`.

FieldError.description:
One field-level failure inside `ErrorResponse.details` (BTY-16b): the
field the caller sent, a stable machine-readable `code` the client maps
to localized text (e.g. `required`, `too_long`, `invalid_format`,
`not_allowed`), and the English server-side `message`.

A list, not a single error, so one 422 can answer with every bad field at
once (BTY-F11) instead of making a form discover them one round-trip at a
time.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable failure code for this field, independent of
the message text.

field.description:
The offending field, as the caller addressed it (e.g. `email` or
`amount`).

message.description: Human-readable, English, server-side detail for this field.

FieldLockedDetails.description:
`details` of a `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` response: every
refused field, the first being the one the top-level `field` names.

GanttBaselineItem.description: One item's planned dates in the baseline.

LockedField.description:
One field a business rule locks for the writer (D-789 §3.5): `effect` is
`hidden` or `disabled`. No value is ever echoed.

PaginatedResponse_CapacityRow.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

items.description:
One row of `GET /api/v1/resources/capacity` — a single resource's
capacity/demand picture over the requested `[from, to]` period (M72).
See `capacity.rs`'s module doc for the exact arithmetic behind each
field — in short: `capacity_hours` is the platform's default business
calendar over the period, net of approved leave; `allocated_hours` is
`resource_allocation.allocation_percent` prorated by date overlap;
`actual_hours` is `project_time_entry.hours`, unrelated to either.

actual_hours.description:
`SUM(hours)` from `project_time_entry` for this resource, entries
dated within `[from, to]` — what was actually logged, independent of
what was planned.

allocated_hours.description:
`SUM(allocation_percent / 100 * capacity_hours * overlap_days /
period_days)` across every `resource_allocation` row overlapping
the period — prorated against the period's nominal (pre-leave)
capacity, not the leave-adjusted figure above; see `capacity.rs`.

capacity_hours.description:
Business-calendar working hours over `[from, to]`, net of any
`resource_availability` leave overlapping the period.

over_allocated.description:
`allocated_hours > capacity_hours` — the resource is committed past
what the period's business calendar (net of leave) can deliver.

resource_name.description:
`user_account.user_name` — `None` for a legacy row with no
username set, same optionality the column itself carries.

utilization_pct.description:
`allocated_hours / capacity_hours * 100`; `0.0` when `capacity_hours`
is `0` (e.g. a period with no working days at all, or a resource on
leave for the whole period) rather than a division-by-zero `NaN`.

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_WorkItemRollupRow.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

items.description:
One row of `GET /api/v1/project/{id}/work-items/rollup` — a work item's
own stored fields plus its point rollup. The client builds the WBS tree
from `parent_work_item_id`, the same flat-list-plus-parent-pointer shape
`entity/document-folder/document-folder-browser.component.ts` already
renders recursively.

is_critical_path.description:
Critical Path Method result — see `critical_path.rs` for the
algorithm and its documented scope (`finish_to_start` dependencies
only). `false`/`None` (not an error) when the project's dependency
graph has a cycle, or when this item isn't part of the dependency
network at all (an isolated item's float is trivially `0`, so it IS
still marked critical — only a genuine cycle degrades to `None`).

points_completed.description:
Sum of `points` over every leaf *descendant* of this node (itself,
if this node is a leaf).

points_own.description:
This node's own `points` value — meaningful only when it is itself a
leaf (`points_total == points_own` in that case); 0 for a
phase/parent row regardless of what its `points` column happens to
hold, per the "parent tasks and phases do not carry their own
progress" rule.

progress_pct.description:
`points_completed / points_total * 100`; `0.0` when `points_total`
is `0` (no leaf descendants yet, e.g. an empty phase).

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PortfolioSummaryResponse.description:
`GET /api/v1/portfolio/{id}/summary` — same rule, rolled up one level
further: every program under the portfolio, and every project under each
of those programs.

ProgramSummaryResponse.description:
`GET /api/v1/program/{id}/summary` — same D-368 read-time-rollup rule as
`ProjectSummaryResponse`, one level up: every number here is computed
fresh from the program's own child projects, never a stored aggregate.

actual_cost_total.description:
Same `is_sensitive`-derived security gate as
`ProjectSummaryResponse::actual_cost` — `None` unless the caller
holds read access to `project_resource_rate`.

weighted_progress_pct.description:
`points_completed / points_total * 100` across every leaf work item
of every project under this program; `0.0` when there are none yet.

ProjectSummaryResponse.description:
`GET /api/v1/project/{id}/summary` — the "Project Control Center" tiles.
Every count/percentage here is computed at read time from the current
state of the project's own fields plus its child work items/issues/change
requests — nothing is a stored/cached rollup (see `work_plan.rs`'s doc
comment for why).

actual_cost.description:
`SUM(time_entry.hours * resource_rate.internal_cost_rate)` across
this project's leaf work items, using each user's most recent rate as
of the entry (falls back to `None`-contributes-nothing when no rate
row exists for that user). Distinct from `budget_consumed` above,
which stays a PM-maintained input — this is computed at read time
from `project_time_entry`/`project_resource_rate`, the same
D-368 rule every other number on this response follows.

`None` (not `0.0`) when the caller lacks read access to
`project_resource_rate` — `internal_cost_rate` is `is_sensitive`,
and this field is derived from it, so it is gated the same way: a
plain `ProjectRead` caller does not automatically see it.

baseline_id.description:
The most recently captured baseline this project's variance fields
are computed against — `None` when no baseline has ever been
captured (`POST /project/{id}/baseline`). See `variance.rs`'s module
doc for exactly what each field below does and does not measure.

budget_at_completion.description:
Budget at Completion — `budget_amount`, unchanged; repeated here so
every EVM figure below reads from one self-contained group.

budget_consumed.description:
PM-maintained for this phase — see the implementation plan's
"Deferred" section (time-entry-driven automation is a follow-up).

cost_performance_index.description:
Cost Performance Index — `EV / AC` (`AC` is `actual_cost` above,
already gated on `project_resource_rate` read access — this
inherits that gate: `None` whenever `actual_cost` is `None`, same as
every other cost-derived field on this response). `> 1` means
under budget for work performed so far, `< 1` means over.

earned_value.description:
Earned Value — `BAC × weighted_progress_pct / 100`, the standard
"budgeted cost of work performed" formula using this project's own
live progress fraction. `None` without a `None` BAC.

estimate_at_completion.description:
Estimate at Completion — `BAC / CPI`, the standard "current cost
performance continues for the rest of the project" projection.

forecast_buffer_days.description:
`target_end_date - forecast_date`, in days. Positive means the
forecast lands before the target (buffer); negative means it lands
after (overrun). `None` unless both dates are present.

forecast_date.description:
`MAX(due_date)` among leaf work items not yet `done` — `None` when
every leaf item is done or the project has no leaf items yet.

health.description:
PM-maintained (`attome_project.health`), not auto-scored — see the
implementation plan's "Deferred" section.

planned_value.description:
Planned Value — `BAC × (baseline points whose planned_due has
already passed) / (baseline points total)`. A simplified,
points-as-progress-measure PV: this crate has no per-task budget to
time-phase (`project_work_item` carries no cost field — see
`baseline.rs`'s own doc comment on why `planned_budget` is always
`NULL`), so points stand in for value the same way `weighted_progress_pct`
already does for EV below. `None` without a baseline or a `None` BAC.

points_blocked.description:
Points belonging to leaf items whose status is `blocked` — a delivery
exposure metric, deliberately not netted out of `points_total` or
counted toward `points_completed`.

schedule_performance_index.description:
Schedule Performance Index — `EV / PV`. `> 1` means ahead of the
baseline's planned pace, `< 1` means behind.

schedule_variance_days.description:
The baseline's own planned finish (`MAX(planned_due)` across its
captured items) minus the live `forecast_date` above, in days.
Positive means the live forecast is ahead of the baseline's plan;
negative means it has slipped behind it. `None` when either date is
missing (no baseline, no baseline item carries a `planned_due`, or
every leaf item is currently `done` so there is no live forecast).

scope_item_count_variance.description:
Active work items now minus active work items captured in the
baseline — positive means scope has grown since the baseline,
negative means it has shrunk (items deactivated/deleted).

variance_at_completion.description:
Variance at Completion — `BAC - EAC`. Positive means the project is
trending to finish under budget.

weighted_progress_pct.description:
`points_completed / points_total * 100`, over the project's leaf work
items only (a phase/parent item never carries its own points — see
`work_plan.rs`). `0.0` when there are no leaf items yet.

work_items_done.description:
Leaf work items only ("actionable" — a phase/parent container is
never itself actionable).

entries.description: The time entries the proposal took.

unrated_users.description: People with billable time but no billable rate, left out.

deliverable_id.description: The accepted deliverable, for a milestone.

until.description:
The last day of time taken, for time and materials (today when
absent).

RuleFailure.description:
One business-rule `error` policy that fired (D-789 §3.3), inside a
`rule_violation` body's `details.rules`. Carries names and the rule's own
message, never a record value.

field.description: The field the policy is attached to, when it names one.

rule_name.description: The rule's display name (its name when it has none).

RuleViolationDetails.description:
`details` of a `rule_violation` response (D-789): the field of the first
failing policy, when it names one, and every blocking `error` policy that
fired, the first (by rule display order) being the one `rule_id` names.

available_after.description: What is left after the spend (negative: over).

Warning.description:
Something the server did that the caller should know about though the
request succeeded (a value truncated, a default applied, a page clamped):
a stable `code` and English `message`. Sent only when there is one.

WorkItemRollupRow.description:
One row of `GET /api/v1/project/{id}/work-items/rollup` — a work item's
own stored fields plus its point rollup. The client builds the WBS tree
from `parent_work_item_id`, the same flat-list-plus-parent-pointer shape
`entity/document-folder/document-folder-browser.component.ts` already
renders recursively.

is_critical_path.description:
Critical Path Method result — see `critical_path.rs` for the
algorithm and its documented scope (`finish_to_start` dependencies
only). `false`/`None` (not an error) when the project's dependency
graph has a cycle, or when this item isn't part of the dependency
network at all (an isolated item's float is trivially `0`, so it IS
still marked critical — only a genuine cycle degrades to `None`).

points_completed.description:
Sum of `points` over every leaf *descendant* of this node (itself,
if this node is a leaf).

points_own.description:
This node's own `points` value — meaningful only when it is itself a
leaf (`points_total == points_own` in that case); 0 for a
phase/parent row regardless of what its `points` column happens to
hold, per the "parent tasks and phases do not carry their own
progress" rule.

progress_pct.description:
`points_completed / points_total * 100`; `0.0` when `points_total`
is `0` (no leaf descendants yet, e.g. an empty phase).

portal_session.name: __Secure-wp_{portal}_session
portal_session.description: A web portal user's session cookie, issued by the portal's sign-in; `{portal}` is the portal's keyword (`wp_{portal}_session` on plain-http local dev). Valid only on that portal's own routes.

s2s_hmac.name: x-s2s-signature
s2s_hmac.description: A system-to-system call, signed. Send `x-s2s-client-id`, `x-s2s-key-id`, `x-s2s-timestamp` (Unix milliseconds, within 300 seconds of the server's clock), `x-s2s-nonce` (single use: a repeat is refused) and `x-s2s-signature`: the hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed by the hex-decoded client secret, of `METHOD`, `PATH_AND_QUERY`, the hex SHA-256 of the body, `TIMESTAMP` and `NONCE`, joined by newlines in that order.

session_cookie.name: __Host-session_token
session_cookie.description: Browser session cookie issued by POST /api/v1/auth/login. Mutating requests additionally require the CSRF conditions enforced by `middleware::csrf`.
